true_positives.matched_candidate:
Delete puts wrong logger in context

Delete builds `log := d.Log.WithValues(name, kind, method)` but then does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `log`. The enriched fields are dropped from the context while Create/Update/List/DeleteCollection propagate the enriched logger, making Delete logs inconsistent and harder to correlate.

true_positives.golden_comment: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Storage and legacy metrics recorded with wrong function

On Storage.Create failure it calls `recordLegacyDuration`, on Storage.Update failure it calls `recordLegacyDuration`, and on async legacy DeleteCollection it calls `recordStorageDuration` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`. Failures are attributed to the wrong store, hiding unified-storage errors and legacy replication errors from dashboards and alerts. Each should record for the store that actually failed.

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Storage duration metric uses object name as kind label

Delete success path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, ...)` where `name` is the object name, while all other calls pass `options.Kind`. If the third parameter is the kind label, passing user-controlled object names creates unbounded Prometheus label cardinality and can OOM the metrics system. Should be `options.Kind`.

false_positives.candidate:
Async legacy failures are never logged

All four async legacy branches only call `recordLegacyDuration/recordStorageDuration` and discard the error without `log.Error`. Operators have no log line to diagnose why legacy and unified storage diverged in mode 3, unlike the previous synchronous code that logged. Should log the legacy error with object identity.

Async legacy writes inherit request context and are cancelled

Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection all do `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx,...)` where ctx is the request context. When the handler returns the request context is cancelled, so the child context is immediately cancelled and the async Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection fails with context canceled. Mode 3's safety backup to legacy therefore never happens. Fix by detaching with context.WithoutCancel/background plus timeout.

Legacy create replicates input object instead of storage result

Create returns `created` from Storage but async replication calls `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` with the original input `obj`. Storage-assigned fields like generated names, UID, resourceVersion and defaults are lost. For generateName creates the two stores will generate different names and diverge, corrupting the legacy backup. Should replicate `created` (deep copy) and not share caller-owned `obj` pointer with an async goroutine.

Mode3 integration tests assume synchronous legacy consistency

The new file/unified mode-3 subtests reuse `doPlaylistTests` which does immediate `getFromBothAPIs` and legacy list checks right after k8s Create/Update. Since mode 3 replicates to legacy asynchronously with up to 10s timeout, the legacy read can race and the test will be flaky or falsely fail. Needs retry/eventual-consistency polling for legacy assertions in mode 3.

Mode3 unit tests do not verify async legacy writes

Tests share one `mock.Mock` for both legacy and storage mocks, set up only storage expectations for Delete/DeleteCollection, and return immediately without waiting for the background goroutine. They cannot prove legacy was or was not called, cannot catch panics from missing mock expectations in the goroutine, and pass even if async replication is broken. Need separate mocks plus Eventually/AssertCalled for legacy.

Update re-invokes UpdatedObjectInfo for legacy causing divergent writes

Update calls `d.Storage.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` with the same objInfo. Each store internally calls `objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` with its own old object, so the transformer runs twice against different old objects and can produce different results or resourceVersion conflicts. The old code fetched the updated object once and reused it via updateWrapper for both stores. Reusing objInfo breaks atomic dual-write consistency.

true_positives.golden_comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing second cache check after acquiring write lock

In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets does double-checked locking: it takes RLock to snapshot entryPointAssetsCache, releases it, then takes Lock to rebuild. After acquiring the write Lock it never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache. If two goroutines both miss the fast path, both will do file/CDN I/O serially and the second will discard/replace the first's result. This wastes work and lets a slow or failing second loader clobber a good value just installed by the first. Re-check if cache became non-nil (in non-Dev mode) after acquiring the write lock and return it without reloading.

true_positives.golden_comment: In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Failed load overwrites good cached assets with nil

In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets unconditionally does entryPointAssetsCache = result at the end, even when readWebAssetsFromFile/CDN failed and result is nil with non-nil err. Combined with concurrent cache misses, a goroutine that succeeds and caches good assets can have its value immediately replaced with nil by another in-flight loader that fails. Subsequent callers then see a miss and must reload/fail. Only assign the global when err == nil and result != nil, preserving the last good value on error.

false_positives.candidate:
Exclusive lock held across file and network I/O blocks all readers

In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() with defer Unlock() before calling readWebAssetsFromFile and readWebAssetsFromCDN, which do filesystem reads and HTTP fetches. While that I/O is in flight, every other caller blocks in RLock on the fast path or Lock on the slow path, so the RWMutex provides no read concurrency and one slow disk/CDN stall stalls all asset lookups. Load into a local variable outside the lock (with double-check/singleflight) and only hold the lock briefly to publish the result.

true_positives.golden_comment: The enableSqlExpressions function has flawed logic that always returns false, effectively disabling SQL expressions unconditionally:
true_positives.matched_candidate:
enableSqlExpressions always returns false with inverted dead logic

In pkg/expr/reader.go enableSqlExpressions computes enabled as !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions) and then returns false in both the if-branch and the fall-through, so it always denies. The negation is backwards and the branch is dead code. The intent to unconditionally disable SQL is achieved, but the confusing logic invites a future cleanup to return enabled, which would silently re-enable DuckDB SQL expressions and reintroduce the CVE-2024-9264 RCE/LFI. Simplify to an unconditional return false with a comment explaining the intentional security disable.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The DB methods NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/db.go return hardcoded 'not implemented' errors after removing the go-duck dependency.

false_positives.candidate:
Legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path not explicitly disabled

In pkg/expr/sql_command.go UnmarshalSQLCommand parses the expression and calls NewSQLCommand with no disabled check, while pkg/expr/reader.go ReadQuery explicitly rejects QueryTypeSQL. The legacy rawNode path is therefore only blocked incidentally because the stubbed sql.TablesList always returns not implemented. Relying on incidental DB failure instead of an explicit deny means restoring a real DB implementation or changing error handling silently re-exposes DuckDB execution and the RCE/LFI vulnerability. Both entry points must explicitly reject SQL expressions.

No regression test that SQL stays disabled regardless of flag

In pkg/expr/reader.go the QueryTypeSQL case is now supposed to always fail, but the PR adds no automated test verifying rejection via ReadQuery and via the legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path with FlagSqlExpressions both on and off. Without a regression test a later refactor can accidentally re-enable DuckDB SQL execution and reintroduce RCE/LFI without detection. Add tests asserting an explicit disabled error in all flag states.

TablesList still attempts DuckDB json_serialize_sql instead of hard-failing

In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go TablesList still builds SELECT json_serialize_sql('...') with strings.Replace quote doubling and fmt.Sprintf and calls RunCommands. With the current stub it fails, but the vulnerable DuckDB-specific code path and injection-prone string interpolation are preserved. If the stub is ever replaced with a real DuckDB connection the RCE/LFI returns. TablesList should return an explicit disabled error immediately without constructing or executing any SQL.

true_positives.golden_comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Removing BuildIndex lock allows duplicate builds for same key

In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go BuildIndex() previously held cacheMu for the whole build and now only locks around b.cache[key] = idx. GetIndex() only takes RLock and returns nil while a build is in flight, so concurrent init workers or concurrent Search-triggered getOrCreateIndex() for the same NamespacedResource will both run bleve.New(), both run the ListIterator builder, both increment IndexTenants, and both write the same file directory for file-backed indexes. The loser is leaked without Close and bleve file creation on the same path can fail with index-exists/lock errors. A coarse lock was slow but correct; the fix needs per-key singleflight, not no lock.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TotalDocs reads cache map without lock

In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go TotalDocs() iterates for _, v := range b.cache with no cacheMu held while BuildIndex() concurrently does b.cache[key] = idx under Lock. In Go concurrent map read and write is a fatal runtime panic, not just a race. With builds now parallelized the window is large, and any concurrent metrics/logging call to TotalDocs during a lazy getOrCreateIndex build can crash the storage server.

false_positives.candidate:
Data races on shared err and counter in concurrent init

In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go init() launches one errgroup goroutine per namespace stat. Each goroutine does totalBatchesIndexed++ and _, _, err = s.build(...) where err is the outer variable from stats, err := GetResourceStats and totalBatchesIndexed is a plain int shared by all workers. With initWorkers > 1 this is concurrent unsynchronized read-modify-write on the same variables while the parent is blocked in group.Wait() and then reassigns err. This is a data race that corrupts the count, loses build errors, and trips the race detector.

History/Origin panic when search not configured

In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go Search() checks if s.search == nil and returns an error, but History() and Origin() unconditionally do s.search.History/Origin. When SearchOptions.Resources is nil, newSearchSupport is skipped and s.search stays nil, which is a valid configuration. Any gRPC History or Origin call then nil-pointer panics and crashes the server instead of returning search-not-configured.

Skipping postgres storage-server test hides init regression

In pkg/server/module_server_test.go the change adds a skip for postgres for TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer. This test exercises storage-server startup, which is exactly what the PR changes from lazy to eager init with DB-dependent GetResourceStats/ListIterator/watch polling. Skipping it means the new startup path is never validated on postgres in CI, so postgres-specific init hangs or failures will not be caught.

Synchronous full reindex in constructor blocks startup

In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go NewResourceServer() now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously, where ctx is the server-lifetime Background context. Init builds every search index via ListIterator over all namespaces before returning. Construction therefore blocks from milliseconds to minutes with no timeout and no way for the caller to cancel, delaying module readiness/health and making any index failure fatal to server creation. Previously reads/writes blocked only on first use; now nothing can start serving until all indexes finish.

Watch goroutine never exits and panics on closed channel

In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go init() starts watchctx := context.Background() and go func() { for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) } } with no ok check and no Done handling. The sql backend poller does defer close(stream) on shutdown. After close, receive returns nil forever in a hot loop and handleEvent dereferences evt.Type on nil, causing nil panic and CPU spin. The goroutine also uses a Background context that is never cancelled on server Stop, so it leaks even on clean shutdown. It must watch server context Done and break on !ok.

true_positives.golden_comment: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Test cleanup removes wrong alias, leaking IDPs

In testCacheIDPByOrg and testCacheIDPForLogin the test creates IDPs in a loop with variable alias (e.g. "org-idp-"+i / "idp-alias-"+i) but registers cleanup as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove with the literal string "alias". That cleanup tries to delete a non-existent IDP named "alias" and never deletes the 10-20 IDPs actually created. The same wrong literal is repeated at lines 381 and 425. Consequence: created brokers leak into the test realm, pollute counts for later assertions on cached login/org queries, and make the suite order-dependent and flaky.

false_negatives.golden_comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.

false_positives.candidate:
getForLogin ignores organization invalidations and serves stale brokers

getByOrganization bypasses cache when isInvalid(cacheKey) || isInvalid(orgId), but the new getForLogin only checks if (isInvalid(cacheKey)). getForLogin results depend on organization state: which orgs exist/are enabled and which IDPs are linked to a given orgId (searchKey is organizationId). When an organization is updated, disabled, or removed its orgId is invalidated but the login query objects keyed by realm+FetchMode are not considered invalid. Subsequent getForLogin calls therefore hit the stale IdentityProviderListQuery and return ID sets containing brokers from disabled/removed orgs or missing newly linked/unlinked brokers. The added isEnabled re-check in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only patches two UI branches, not the provider contract, so direct callers of getForLogin get stale login options.

update/remove dereferences null IDP model causing NPE

update() does IdentityProviderModel idpById = getById(model.getInternalId()) which returns null when the id is null or not found, then unconditionally calls registerIDPInvalidation(idpById) which calls idp.getInternalId() and idp.getAlias(). remove() has the same pattern with storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) followed by registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) when the alias key is invalidated. If the alias/id does not exist, storedIdp/idpById is null and the call throws NullPointerException. Consequence: updating or removing a missing broker fails with a 500 NPE instead of returning false / proper not-found handling.

true_positives.golden_comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getBouncyCastleProvider returns non-BouncyCastle provider

In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 61 getBouncyCastleProvider contract states it returns the BouncyCastle security provider (FIPS or non-FIPS). Implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), typically SUN or SunJSSE, not BouncyCastle. Callers using the returned Provider for BC-specific algorithms will get wrong behavior or NoSuchAlgorithmException. Like WildFlyElytronProvider it should return null when BC is not used.

true_positives.golden_comment: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations
true_positives.matched_candidate:
New abstract order() breaks external CryptoProvider implementations

In common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java line 44 the interface adds abstract method int order(). Any third-party CryptoProvider implementation compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError/NoSuchMethodError and will fail to compile against the new interface. This is a binary and source incompatible change. It should be a default method e.g. default int order() { return 0; } to preserve compatibility.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.

false_positives.candidate:
AuthzClient.create poisons global CryptoIntegration singleton

In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/AuthzClient.java line 95 create() calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()). CryptoIntegration holds a static volatile singleton initialized only once and never re-evaluated for a different ClassLoader. If authz-client initializes first with a ClassLoader that only sees the fallback AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100), a later server init that could see Default/FIPS/Elytron (order 200) is ignored. In modular runtimes where visibility differs per loader this permanently locks in the weak provider and breaks server crypto.

Same order for all server providers makes selection nondeterministic

In common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java line 57 detectProvider sorts by order reversed and picks element 0. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, AuthzClientCryptoProvider returns 100. For equal order ServiceLoader order is classpath dependent, so a classpath containing both FIPS and non-FIPS/default providers now silently picks an arbitrary one instead of failing fast as before. Previously multiple providers threw IllegalStateException. Silently picking non-FIPS when FIPS is required (or vice versa) is a compliance and security failure and masks misconfiguration.

Test reuses P-256 key for ES384/ES512 and only checks round-trip

In authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java line 42 a single KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() (default P-256) is reused for ES256 (64 bytes), ES384 (96 bytes) and ES512 (132 bytes). Signing P-256 keys with SHA384/SHA512 still yields P-256 sized DER that is zero-padded to larger lengths, so the test passes without exercising real P-384/P-521 sizes. The test also only asserts asn1->concat->asn1 round-trip equality and never verifies with Signature.verify or known vectors, so truncation, leading-zero and negative-value bugs are not detected.

concatenatedRSToASN1DER lacks input length validation

In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 103 concatenatedRSToASN1DER splits signature into r/s with len=signLength/2 and System.arraycopy without checking signature.length==signLength. A short or long input throws unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of declared IOException, and odd signLength silently drops a byte. Callers expecting IOException handling will get unexpected runtime exceptions.

integerToBytes silently mangles negative and oversized integers

In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 151 integerToBytes converts DER INTEGER BigInteger to fixed-length bytes by truncating leading bytes if too long and zero-padding if too short. It does not reject negative values or values >= 2^(8*qLength). E.g. DER -1 (bytes 0xFF) becomes 32 bytes of 0x00..FF (255), and an oversized r/s is truncated to low bytes. Invalid out-of-range signature values are thus transformed into different in-range values instead of throwing IOException, hiding malformed signatures and enabling signature malleability.

readSequence does not enforce exact length match

In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java line 57 readSequence loops while(length>0) subtracting each child TLV length from the declared SEQUENCE content length but never checks that the remainder is exactly zero. If children total more than declared, length goes negative and the loop exits silently returning e.g. 2 elements. Malformed DER with trailing/mismatched lengths is accepted as valid instead of throwing IOException, which can cause invalid ECDSA signatures to be accepted by asn1derToConcatenatedRS.

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Removal listener disabled for V2 leaves orphan authz resources

registerListener now only runs when feature ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. When only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent are ignored and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException so there is no alternative path. Deleting a client in V2 therefore leaves its per-client authorization resource and associated policies orphaned in the store.

true_positives.golden_comment: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getClientsWithPermission returns type resource as client id

getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType for type Clients and adds every granted resource.getName() to the result. The all-type resource itself has type Clients and name Clients, so it is also visited. If the all-clients permission is granted, the returned set contains the bogus id Clients instead of real client ids, and per-client checks do not consider the all-type grant. Callers filtering clients by this set get wrong results.

true_positives.golden_comment: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing null check before findByResource causes NPE

In hasPermission(ClientModel,String) when no per-client resource is found the code loads the all-clients resource via getResourceTypeResource, which can return null if the Clients type resource is missing, and then immediately calls findByResource(server, resource) with that value. Passing null throws NullPointerException/IllegalArgumentException instead of returning false, turning a permission check into a 500 error.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

false_positives.candidate:
Duplicate scopes not de-duplicated on init

In AdminPermissionsSchema.init the code collects ScopeRepresentation objects into a Set to get rid of duplicities when USERS and CLIENTS share scopes (manage, view, map-roles). ScopeRepresentation does not implement equals/hashCode by name, so the Set contains one object per occurrence (11 objects for 8 distinct names). The realm init then tries to create duplicate scopes named manage/view/map-roles, which can fail or create duplicates for every new realm with admin permissions enabled.

Per-client check ignores all-clients grant when specific resource exists

ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String) looks up the per-client resource by client id and only if it is null falls back to evaluating the all-clients resource named Clients. If a per-client resource exists (created for any prior per-client permission) the method evaluates only that resource and never evaluates the all-clients resource. An admin granted manage/view/configure/map-roles on all clients is therefore incorrectly denied on any client that happens to have a per-client resource, breaking the documented all-clients fallback.

Wrong Javadoc for requireView methods

The interface documents void requireView() as Returns true if canView() returns true and void requireViewClientScopes() as Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true. Both methods return void and throw ForbiddenException on denial. The copy-pasted return documentation misleads implementers and callers about the contract.

getResourceName has no handling for Clients type

getResourceName special-cases the Users type to return All users or the username for a user resource, but has no branch for the new Clients type. For client permissions it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not set for auto-created client resources (name is the client UUID). Permission listings for clients will show null/blank instead of the clientId.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Incorrect method call for exit codes. The picocli.exit() method calls System.exit() directly, which is problematic:
Need to add changelog/release notes documenting the exit code change and migration guidance

false_positives.candidate:
Default upgrade-strategy test never enables rolling-updates feature

In createInitialDeployment the method returns early when updateStrategy is null without configuring spec.features.enabled to include rolling-updates, while the RECREATE path does configure it. The guide added in the same PR states the Operator requires the rolling-updates preview feature or it will fail. As a result the parameterized cases with null/default strategy run without the required feature, so they fail for the wrong reason and never exercise the intended default-strategy upgrade path. The feature setup must happen before the early return for all strategies.

Docs claim Operator fails without rolling-updates, breaking all existing CRs

The added CAUTION says while in preview the rolling-updates feature must be enabled otherwise the Keycloak Operator will fail. Rolling-updates is a new feature so every existing Keycloak CR lacks it. Failing all reconciliations until every CR is edited is an unnecessary breaking change. The compatible behavior is to fall back to pre-existing behavior when the feature is disabled and only fail the specific CR that requests the preview update strategy without the flag. As written the docs either mandate an overly broad outage or are inaccurate since no operator code in the PR scopes the failure.

Failure exit codes for update-compatibility tool are not verified

The documented contract for automation is the exit code: 0 rolling possible, 3 recreate required, 4 feature rolling-updates disabled. This PR renumbers RECREATE from 4 to 3 and adds 4 for disabled, but testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the stderr text and never asserts exit code 4, and testWrongVersions never asserts exit code 3. Only the happy path asserts exit code 0. A regression that prints the correct message but returns the wrong code, including 0 on failure, would pass tests and break scripts and operator logic that branches on the exit code.

true_positives.golden_comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Global canManage() grants manage on VIEW

In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70, canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), identical to canView(). This lets an admin with only VIEW on the all-groups resource pass requireManage(), e.g. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup which requires global manage. Consequence is privilege escalation: read-only group viewers can create top-level groups. Fix is to check only MANAGE for global manage, matching per-group canManage(group) which correctly checks only MANAGE.

true_positives.golden_comment: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource UUID instead of group ID

In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122-123, findByType iterates group resources but calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId()) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). Per AdminPermissionsSchema group resources are named by groupId (resolveGroup returns groupId) while getId() is the internal authz UUID, so findByName lookup misses and the granted set contains authz UUIDs not group IDs. UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource then filter user searches and counts by UserModel.GROUPS with bogus IDs, returning empty or wrong user sets and breaking pagination.

false_positives.candidate:
Existing realms never get Groups resource and scopes

In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:250, init() returns early if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. readSequence does not enforce exact length match

In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java line 57 readSequence loops while(length>0) subtracting each child TLV length from the declared SEQUENCE content length but never checks that the remainder is exactly zero. If children total more than declared, length goes negative and the loop exits silently returning e.g. 2 elements. Malformed DER with trailing/mismatched lengths is accepted as valid instead of throwing IOException, which can cause invalid ECDSA signatures to be accepted by asn1derToConcatenatedRS.

integerToBytes silently mangles negative and oversized integers

In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 151 integerToBytes converts DER INTEGER BigInteger to fixed-length bytes by truncating leading bytes if too long and zero-padding if too short. It does not reject negative values or values >= 2^(8*qLength). E.g. DER -1 (bytes 0xFF) becomes 32 bytes of 0x00..FF (255), and an oversized r/s is truncated to low bytes. Each goroutine does totalBatchesIndexed++ and _, _, err = s.build(...) where err is the outer variable from stats, err := GetResourceStats and totalBatchesIndexed is a plain int shared by all workers. With initWorkers > 1 this is concurrent unsynchronized read-modify-write on the same variables while the parent is blocked in group.Wait() and then reassigns err. This is a data race that corrupts the count, loses build errors, and trips the race detector.

Watch goroutine never exits and panics on closed channel

In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go init() starts watchctx := context.Background() and go func() { for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) } } with no ok check and no Done handling. The sql backend poller does defer close(stream) on shutdown. After close, receive returns nil forever in a hot loop and handleEvent dereferences evt.Type on nil, causing nil panic and CPU spin. The goroutine also uses a Background context that is never cancelled on server Stop, so it leaks even on clean shutdown. It must watch server context Done and break on !ok.

History/Origin panic when search not configured

In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go Search() checks if s.search == nil and returns an error, but History() and Origin() unconditionally do s.search.History/Origin. When SearchOptions.Resources is nil, newSearchSupport is skipped and s.search stays nil, which is a valid configuration. Any gRPC History or Origin call then nil-pointer panics and crashes the server instead of returning search-not-configured.

Synchronous full reindex in constructor blocks startup

In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go NewResourceServer() now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously, where ctx is the server-lifetime Background context. Init builds every search index via ListIterator over all namespaces before returning. Construction therefore blocks from milliseconds to minutes with no timeout and no way for the caller to cancel, delaying module readiness/health and making any index failure fatal to server creation. Previously reads/writes blocked only on first use; now nothing can start serving until all indexes finish.

Skipping postgres storage-server test hides init regression

In pkg/server/module_server_test.go the change adds a skip for postgres for TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer. This test exercises storage-server startup, which is exactly what the PR changes from lazy to eager init with DB-dependent GetResourceStats/ListIterator/watch polling. Skipping it means the new startup path is never validated on postgres in CI, so postgres-specific init hangs or failures will not be caught.

false_positives.candidate:
Queue.shutdown does not exist on Python <3.13, shutdown hangs

FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls q.shutdown(immediate=False). queue.Queue.shutdown was added in Python 3.13. On older runtimes this raises AttributeError, which is caught and logged per-queue, leaving workers blocked forever in work_queue.get(). Worker.join(timeout=5.0) then times out and close()/terminate() never actually stops workers. Consequence is leaked daemon threads and hung consumer shutdown/rebalance.

Offsets marked complete even when processing fails

OrderedQueueWorker.run calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in a finally block after result_processor. Any exception is logged and swallowed, then the offset is still marked done, so get_committable_offsets advances past failures. This contradicts the class docstring 'Only commits offsets after successful processing' and bypasses Arroyo DLQ handling, which requires the strategy to raise. Consequence is silent data loss: transient DB/cache errors cause uptime results to be skipped and committed as if successful.

Unbounded queues provide no backpressure

FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and submit() does add_offset then non-blocking put. The docstring claims 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up' but there is no bound, so if Kafka polling outpaces workers the process enqueues unboundedly. Consequence is unbounded memory growth and OOM when a queue backs up, plus unbounded growth of OffsetTracker sets.

Offsets committed from background thread

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy spawns a commit_thread that every second calls get_committable_offsets then commit_function, which in result_consumer.py calls Arroyo commit(). That Commit callback is owned by the StreamProcessor poll thread and tied to partition assignment. Calling it concurrently from a background thread races with rebalance/close/terminate, committing revoked partitions or committing while Arroyo is tearing down the strategy. Consequence is commit errors, lost commits, or duplicates.

Factory-shared queue pool is shut down by per-assignment strategy

ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and hands the same object to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy returned by create_with_partitions. But SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate() calls queue_pool.shutdown(), and factory.shutdown() also shuts it down. After a rebalance the old strategy kills workers/queues still referenced by the factory, so the next strategy reuses a dead pool and stops processing, while multiple live strategies would share one OffsetTracker with multiple commit loops. Consequence is a stalled consumer after the first rebalance.

close() loses final commits; terminate() leaks commit thread

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close sets shutdown_event then joins commit_thread before draining workers via queue_pool.shutdown(). Offsets completed while workers drain after the commit thread exited are never committed. terminate sets the event but never joins the commit thread at all, leaving a daemon thread that can keep calling commit_function after partitions are revoked. Consequence is duplicate reprocessing on restart and commit-after-revoke errors.

Committable scan iterates full offset range

OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets computes min/max of all_offsets then loops for offset in range(start, max_offset+1). With a sparse gap the loop cost is proportional to the numeric gap, not the number of tracked offsets. A single missing offset with a large max can cause millions of iterations every second per partition. It should iterate the sorted tracked set instead. Consequence is CPU spikes and stalled commit loop under gaps.

FilteredPayload handled via AssertionError

ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload starts with assert not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload). SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit passes message.payload straight to this decoder, so every filtered message raises AssertionError, logs 'Failed to decode' or 'Error submitting message to queue', then is marked complete via the exception path. Filtered messages should return None explicitly without assert/exception. Consequence is noisy exception logs for normal filtered traffic and exception-driven control flow.

wait_until_empty and stats ignore in-flight work

FixedQueuePool.get_stats sums q.qsize() and wait_until_empty polls total_items==0. qsize only counts items still queued, not the item already removed by Queue.get() and being processed by a worker with its offset still outstanding. wait_until_empty therefore can return True while work is still in flight and offsets uncommitted. Consequence is premature test synchronization and any production use would incorrectly assume quiescence.

Hash distribution test is flaky

test_different_groups_distributed asserts that 20 keys group0..group19 with hash(key)%3 hit all 3 queues. Python string hash is salted per process, so hitting all buckets is probabilistic, not guaranteed. The test can fail on some hash seeds despite correct code. It should mock hashing or assert consistency only, not full coverage. Consequence is flaky CI.

Queue-depth assertion races with workers

test_stats_reporting submits 10 items then immediately asserts get_stats total_items>0. Workers start in FixedQueuePool.__init__ and can drain the unbounded queues before the assertion runs, making total_items==0 and failing the test nondeterministically. The test needs to pause workers or poll until expected state instead of asserting transient queue depth. Consequence is flaky CI.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours check ignores duration and inverts multi-block logic

The `workingHours.find` check computes both `start` and `end` from `slotStartTime.hour()*60+minute`, ignoring `eventLength` and `slotEndTime`, so a slot that starts inside but ends outside working hours passes. It also returns true if ANY block does not contain the slot, instead of checking if NO block contains it. With two blocks on the same weekday (e.g. morning and afternoon) a valid slot inside one block is outside the other and is marked unavailable, while a weekday with no matching `days` entry returns falsy and is treated as available. Fixed hosts can appear available when they have no hours and unavailable when they have split hours.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dayjs objects compared with === never match

At line 114 the code does `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect a full-day unavailable date override. `===` on objects compares references, so two separately created Dayjs instances are never equal. The branch never runs, `dateOverrideExist` becomes true but `find` returns falsy, and the function falls through to `return true`. A day marked unavailable by a date override is therefore reported as available, including for fixed hosts in round-robin events, allowing bookings that should be blocked.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: comparing separately created Dayjs objects with === checks reference identity rather than date values, so the comparison always fails. The candidate adds consequences but matches the golden issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Date-override containment misses end overrun and exact boundary

The override test only rejects a slot if `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`. It never checks `slotEndTime > overrideEnd`, and uses `isAfter` instead of same-or-after for the end. A slot starting inside the override but ending after it (e.g. override 10:00-11:00, slot 10:30-11:30) does not match either condition, `find` returns falsy, and with `dateOverrideExist=true` the function returns true. Bookings can extend beyond the override window, and a slot starting exactly at override end is also considered inside.

Date-override day match mixes local and UTC timezones

`utcOffset` is derived with `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()*-1` then applied to `dayjs(date.start)` which is parsed in server-local time, while `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()`. Formatting both with `YYYY MM DD` compares a local-calendar day to a UTC-calendar day. Unless the server runs in UTC the day equality and the shifted start/end comparisons can be off by a day, causing overrides to apply to the wrong date or be ignored for organizers/invitees in other zones.

Offsets derived from Date.toString() parsing are fragile

Organizer and invitee offsets are computed as `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(zone).utcOffset()`. `Date.toString()` is locale and server-timezone dependent (e.g. includes local abbrev) and is not a stable input for dayjs parsing with a zone. It can parse incorrectly or yield Invalid Date/NaN, producing NaN start/end minutes and dropping all slots or shifting them. It should use `dayjs(override.start).tz(zone)` directly without stringifying.

Active override filtered by wall-encoded instant not true instant

The filter `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, ...)` uses the stored override Date directly, but that Date encodes organizer wall time as UTC hours. The true UTC instant is wall minus organizer offset. Near midnight a wall time and its true instant fall on different invitee calendar days (e.g. true 23:30 UTC with +5:30 organizer becomes 05:00 wall next day). The override can then be attached to the wrong invitee day or missed entirely for invitees in distant timezones.

Availability check ignores variable duration

Slots are generated with `eventLength: input.duration || eventType.length` but `availabilityCheckProps` hard-codes `eventLength: eventType.length`. For event types with multiple duration options the `checkIfIsAvailable` busy/override/working-hours window uses the wrong length, so a longer selected duration can be reported as available when it overruns an override, working hours, or busy block, or vice versa.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

false_positives.candidate:
Public findMany API removed without caller migration

The old InsightsBookingService exposed findMany(findManyArgs) that applied authorization plus filter conditions via Prisma findMany. This PR deletes findMany and replaces it with getBaseConditions() returning Prisma.Sql. Only the service and its test are changed, no callers are updated. Any existing production caller that still calls service.findMany() will fail at compile time or throw TypeError at runtime, breaking insights endpoints.

Authorization SQL fragment with top-level OR is not parenthesized

buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition return a fragment of the form (team condition) OR (user condition) with no outer parentheses, and getBaseConditions returns that fragment bare when there is no filter. SQL AND binds tighter than OR, so a caller composing WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <extra> gets teamCond OR (userCond AND extra) instead of (teamCond OR userCond) AND extra. Extra restrictions like date ranges or additional checks are then bypassed for one branch, returning rows that should have been excluded.

Event-type filter OR fragment is not parenthesized

buildFilterConditions for eventTypeId returns ("eventTypeId" = $1) OR ("eventParentId" = $1) with no outer parentheses. getBaseConditions happens to wrap it, but getFilterConditions is public and returns bare OR. Any direct use as WHERE ${filter} AND <other> evaluates as A OR (B AND other) because AND has higher precedence, producing wrong filter results.

Those arrays come from findAllByParentId and findAllByTeamIds which have no ORDER BY, so database return order is not guaranteed. Since = ANY is order-insensitive, the implementation is correct regardless of order but the toEqual on Sql values will flake when the DB returns a different order.

It also runs full validations and callbacks for a counter update. Use an atomic counter update such as increment_counter/update_counters instead of read-modify-write.

After the server rejects an email the computed property does not recompute, so the inline invalid message is not shown and submitDisabled is not updated until the user edits the email field. The dependent key should be rejectedEmails.[].

The golden comment says it may 'never terminate correctly', while the candidate notes it runs up to 5 iterations. The core issue is the same: a stale size check in the loop.

false_positives.candidate:
In-place downsize overwrites source file

ImageMagick convert reading and writing the same path is unsafe, and if conversion fails the original upload bytes are already truncated or destroyed. Upload.create_for then stores the corrupt/truncated file, causing permanent data loss for that upload. A separate temp output file that is only moved into place on success is required.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours check ignores duration and inverts multi-block logic

The `workingHours.find` check computes both `start` and `end` from `slotStartTime.hour()*60+minute`, ignoring `eventLength` and `slotEndTime`, so a slot that starts inside but ends outside working hours passes. It also returns true if ANY block does not contain the slot, instead of checking if NO block contains it. With two blocks on the same weekday (e.g. morning and afternoon) a valid slot inside one block is outside the other and is marked unavailable, while a weekday with no matching `days` entry returns falsy and is treated as available. Fixed hosts can appear available when they have no hours and unavailable when they have split hours.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate says both start and end are computed from slotStartTime, ignoring slotEndTime. That is the same bug the golden comment describes. The extra points about the multi-block logic do not change this match.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dayjs objects compared with === never match

At line 114 the code does `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect a full-day unavailable date override. `===` on objects compares references, so two separately created Dayjs instances are never equal. The branch never runs, `dateOverrideExist` becomes true but `find` returns falsy, and the function falls through to `return true`. A day marked unavailable by a date override is therefore reported as available, including for fixed hosts in round-robin events, allowing bookings that should be blocked.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same bug: comparing Dayjs objects with === checks references rather than values, so the comparison always returns false. The candidate points to the same comparison of date.start and date.end and adds its downstream impact.

false_positives.candidate:
Date-override containment misses end overrun and exact boundary

The override test only rejects a slot if `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`. It never checks `slotEndTime > overrideEnd`, and uses `isAfter` instead of same-or-after for the end. A slot starting inside the override but ending after it (e.g. override 10:00-11:00, slot 10:30-11:30) does not match either condition, `find` returns falsy, and with `dateOverrideExist=true` the function returns true. Bookings can extend beyond the override window, and a slot starting exactly at override end is also considered inside.

Date-override day match mixes local and UTC timezones

`utcOffset` is derived with `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()*-1` then applied to `dayjs(date.start)` which is parsed in server-local time, while `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()`. Formatting both with `YYYY MM DD` compares a local-calendar day to a UTC-calendar day. Unless the server runs in UTC the day equality and the shifted start/end comparisons can be off by a day, causing overrides to apply to the wrong date or be ignored for organizers/invitees in other zones.

Offsets derived from Date.toString() parsing are fragile

Organizer and invitee offsets are computed as `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(zone).utcOffset()`. `Date.toString()` is locale and server-timezone dependent (e.g. includes local abbrev) and is not a stable input for dayjs parsing with a zone. It can parse incorrectly or yield Invalid Date/NaN, producing NaN start/end minutes and dropping all slots or shifting them. It should use `dayjs(override.start).tz(zone)` directly without stringifying.

Active override filtered by wall-encoded instant not true instant

The filter `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, ...)` uses the stored override Date directly, but that Date encodes organizer wall time as UTC hours. The true UTC instant is wall minus organizer offset. Near midnight a wall time and its true instant fall on different invitee calendar days (e.g. true 23:30 UTC with +5:30 organizer becomes 05:00 wall next day). The override can then be attached to the wrong invitee day or missed entirely for invitees in distant timezones.

Availability check ignores variable duration

Slots are generated with `eventLength: input.duration || eventType.length` but `availabilityCheckProps` hard-codes `eventLength: eventType.length`. For event types with multiple duration options the `checkIfIsAvailable` busy/override/working-hours window uses the wrong length, so a longer selected duration can be reported as available when it overruns an override, working hours, or busy block, or vice versa.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

false_positives.candidate:
Public findMany API removed without caller migration

The old InsightsBookingService exposed findMany(findManyArgs) that applied authorization plus filter conditions via Prisma findMany. This PR deletes findMany and replaces it with getBaseConditions() returning Prisma.Sql. Only the service and its test are changed, no callers are updated. Any existing production caller that still calls service.findMany() will fail at compile time or throw TypeError at runtime, breaking insights endpoints.

Authorization SQL fragment with top-level OR is not parenthesized

buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition return a fragment of the form (team condition) OR (user condition) with no outer parentheses, and getBaseConditions returns that fragment bare when there is no filter. SQL AND binds tighter than OR, so a caller composing WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <extra> gets teamCond OR (userCond AND extra) instead of (teamCond OR userCond) AND extra. Extra restrictions like date ranges or additional checks are then bypassed for one branch, returning rows that should have been excluded.

Event-type filter OR fragment is not parenthesized

buildFilterConditions for eventTypeId returns ("eventTypeId" = $1) OR ("eventParentId" = $1) with no outer parentheses. getBaseConditions happens to wrap it, but getFilterConditions is public and returns bare OR. Any direct use as WHERE ${filter} AND <other> evaluates as A OR (B AND other) because AND has higher precedence, producing wrong filter results.

Org scope test assumes deterministic order for ANY arrays

The org-scope test asserts exact equality with Prisma.sql containing team ID array [org, team, team2, team3] and user ID array [user, user2, user3]. Those arrays come from findAllByParentId and findAllByTeamIds which have no ORDER BY, so database return order is not guaranteed. Since = ANY is order-insensitive, the implementation is correct regardless of order but the toEqual on Sql values will flake when the DB returns a different order.

Consequence is the exactly-once guarantee for backup codes is broken under concurrency.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same problem. Backup codes are read and checked, then written back in a separate step. Two concurrent logins with the same code can both pass the check, which breaks one-time use.

false_positives.candidate:

authorize() only verifies the password when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121), but the backup-code branch is taken whenever `credentials.backupCode` is truthy without requiring totpCode to be empty. An attacker who knows a valid backup code can send email + valid backupCode + any dummy totpCode, which skips password verification and then succeeds on backup-code check alone without ever verifying password or TOTP. Consequence is second-factor-only login: password is not required, so a leaked or guessed 10-char backup code alone yields account takeover.

Backup codes stored with reversible encryption instead of hash

Backup codes are persisted with symmetricEncrypt, which is reversible with CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY, and later decrypted for comparison. Unlike the TOTP secret which must be reversible, backup codes only need comparison and should be one-way hashed like passwords. Consequence is that any database plus encryption-key compromise exposes all long-lived backup codes in plaintext, allowing persistent bypass of the authenticator.

Lost-access toggle button unintentionally submits disable form

The Lost access / Go back button is rendered inside the Form that handles disable but has no type="button" and no preventDefault, so browsers treat it as type submit. Clicking it to switch between TOTP and backup-code inputs also triggers handleDisable with empty codes. Consequence is spurious disable requests and confusing incorrect-code errors when the user only intended to switch modes.

Download backup-codes button also submits enable form

The download link and Button are inside the Form whose submit handler verifies the TOTP code, but unlike the Copy and Close buttons which call preventDefault, the Download button has no type button handling or preventDefault. Clicking Download therefore also submits the enable form with the stale totpCode. Consequence is duplicate enable API calls on every download, possible error states on the backup-codes screen where no error is displayed.

Throwing Error instead of JSON response breaks client handling

When the encryption key is missing or the 2FA secret is missing the handler does throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError) instead of returning res.status(500).json({error}). An uncaught throw in a Next.js API route produces a non-JSON 500 page, while the modal client always does await response.json() and expects {error}. Consequence is unhandled exceptions, failed JSON parsing, and generic UI failure instead of a structured error.

Used codes nulled not removed so exhaustion never detected

After a successful backup-code login the code sets backupCodes[index] = null and re-encrypts the same-length array. After all 10 codes are used the column is still a non-null JSON array of nulls, so the MissingBackupCodes check for !user.backupCodes never fires and later attempts always return IncorrectBackupCode. Consequence is stale data accumulates and users get a misleading error with no signal that they are out of codes and must re-generate via disable/enable.

No coverage for login or disable with backup code

This PR adds backup-code authentication in next-auth, the login page Lost access flow, and the disable-with-backup-code endpoint, but the e2e only exercises download, copy, and close of the backup-codes dialog and explicitly leaves a TODO for login plus disabling with backup. Consequence is single-use invalidation, password interaction, and IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes paths ship untested.
